Reference city interruption and gameplay dependency recovery

Date: October 16, 2026. Project: ForgeMCPDev, UE 5.6.1.

Observed crash

The original live Editor ([session id redacted]) crashed during PIE startup from /Game/Levels/NewMap_PCGTest.NewMap_PCGTest. The log records PIE world creation at 21:56:03 UTC and a null-read access violation at 21:56:35 UTC. The stack enters UAnimBlueprintExtension_PropertyAccess::HandleStartCompilingClass, Blueprint compilation, package loading and UGameInstance::CreateGameModeForURL. The crash context does not flag an out-of-memory condition. This evidence points to a gameplay/animation dependency problem; it does not establish a GPU or city geometry fault, nor exclude every possible concurrent factor.

Immediately before the crash, the log reports absent EnhancedInput classes, ControlRig/RigVM classes, AnimationData, and an unknown AnimNode_ControlRig structure in ABP_Unarmed. The project explicitly disables engine plugins by default while selecting BP_ThirdPersonGameMode as its global default game mode. The required gameplay plugins were not explicitly enabled.

Changes

  • Preserved the original descriptor at Saved/ReferenceCity_20261016_v1/CrashRecovery/ForgeMCPDev.before_dependency_fix.uproject.
  • Enabled EnhancedInput, ControlRig, AnimationData and FullBodyIK in the project descriptor. Existing plugin entries and gameplay asset bytes are preserved. FullBodyIK supplies the PBIK structures used by CR_Mannequin_FootIK.
  • Stopped further city import work. The interrupted transfer 90305d885d8f43a5879551395a1fa1b4 ended during staging with disconnected; no native import-start event or native import report exists for that transfer. Its receipt is retained and must not be blindly replayed.
  • Updated the importer to require a freshly inspected explicit target session and save the level/external actor packages after each successful placement, before the next import can invalidate a save preview.

Preserved city work

Nineteen city static-mesh packages were inventoried on disk under /Game/ReferenceCity_20261016_v1/. This is partial Unreal import completion. The full 37-mesh Blender source, overview, closer render and source reload report remain under Saved/ReferenceCity_20261016_v1/. The scene contains 5,168 generated building masses over ten manually interpreted districts, using an assumed three metres per image pixel. It is an approximate reference-based scene, not a surveyed 1:1 reconstruction, photorealistic completion or a native PCG/spline implementation.

The attempted mid-import level checkpoint was rejected as stale. Consequently, placement persistence cannot be inferred from import receipts or mesh files. Reinspect the reloaded target level before restoring missing actors.

Validation evidence and remaining steps

Validation logs and package hashes are retained in Saved/ReferenceCity_20261016_v1/CrashRecovery/. Initial commandlet attempts failed to apply their intended allowlist due path handling and native argument parsing; those diagnostic processes were stopped without saving assets. The corrected targeted run loaded/compiled the Third Person game mode, character and ABP_Unarmed without the original crash. It exposed missing PBIK types in the dependent foot-IK rig, leading to the additional FullBodyIK dependency fix.

The final targeted gameplay/foot-IK compile result is recorded in BlueprintValidation_WithFootIK.log and footik_exit_code.txt; inspect both before claiming validation success. This commandlet does not test interactive PIE, GPU rendering, collision, World Partition streaming or city performance.

The final log confirms successful compilation of BP_ThirdPersonGameMode, BP_ThirdPersonCharacter, ABP_Unarmed and CR_Mannequin_FootIK, with zero Blueprint compile errors, warnings or failed loads. The engine reports zero errors and nine startup warnings: missing ACL animation compression presets and a duplicate DDC cache path. Those warnings remain outside this minimal dependency correction. The tracked gameplay package hashes match before/after the diagnostic runs; original plugin entries compare unchanged, with only the four required entries appended.

The user's replacement Editor launched before the descriptor fix. A fresh Editor startup is required to load the newly enabled dependencies. Reconnect using a live session, verify project and NewMap_PCGTest, inspect saved city placements, then resume only the missing imports and placements with per-placement checkpoints.
